issue_request: FHIR-15133 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core StructureDefinition correction for STU3. It reported that eld-16's ElementDefinition.sliceName regular expression had been updated into a broken form and asked for a corrected character class for proper sliceName tokens.
initial_application: The Jira comment says the change was applied in svn revision 13056. Git history preserves that as a03dfbf6f901f36bab3f618193c7fcb9bbbd5a51, which changed source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml for #15133 and replaced the affected eld-16 FHIRPath and XPath regex cells. An earlier same-invariant issue, FHIR-13771, had already removed the illegal escaped underscore in commit 1709591740fd1ffd8c82b3a874bfe4ba3bca021b.
additional_context: ElementDefinition is an active datatype in the current build configuration, and source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml is the active spreadsheet source for the invariant. The current eld-16 row allows slash, hyphen, underscore, square brackets, and @, preserving the #15133 correction plus the later GF#14389 tweak in 116056cc35dadc8649cab84578377258a304b857. Current generated history snapshots for release4/release4b/release5 carry the same corrected pattern. Jira search only found the earlier FHIR-13771 same-invariant issue, and direct Zulip/Confluence searches found no issue-specific conflicting rationale.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current active source no longer has the broken regex reported by FHIR-15133, and reverting to the exact Jira-suggested character class would remove the later accepted @ allowance.
